ticket: My API calls started returning 429 errors about 2 hours ago. We haven't changed anything on our end.
agent_response: HTTP 429 means you're hitting our rate limit. Before I dig in, can you share: (1) roughly how many requests per minute you're sending, (2) which endpoint is hitting the limit, and (3) whether this started suddenly or built up gradually? That will help me determine whether your usage crossed a threshold or whether we have a misconfigured limit on your account.

ticket: Our webhook deliveries are failing intermittently. Maybe 20% of events don't reach our endpoint.
agent_response: Intermittent webhook failures at 20% are almost always a signature validation issue or a timeout on your endpoint's side. To narrow it down: can you check your server logs for the failing events and tell me (1) what HTTP status code your endpoint is returning, and (2) whether the failures cluster around specific event types or are random across all events? If you're seeing 200s on your end but we show failures, that points to a signature mismatch. If you're seeing timeouts, we need to look at your endpoint response time.

ticket: The sync between our CRM and your platform stopped working yesterday. No error message shown.
agent_response: Silent sync failures usually fall into a few buckets: an expired OAuth token, a permission scope that was removed, or a field mapping that broke due to a schema change on either side. I don't want to guess — can you tell me what changed around when the sync stopped? A recent password change, a CRM update, or anyone adjusting integration settings would all be relevant. Also, check Settings > Integrations > CRM and tell me if the connection status shows 'Connected' or something else.

ticket: Users on iOS are getting logged out randomly. Android users are fine.
agent_response: iOS-only session issues with Android unaffected points to something platform-specific — either how iOS handles background refresh and token expiry, or a different authentication flow for iOS. I'm not certain yet which. Can you tell me: (1) what version of your iOS app they're running, (2) whether this happens after a specific action or seemingly at random, and (3) whether it started after your last iOS release or has been ongoing? That will help me determine whether this is a token refresh bug or something in our session handling for iOS clients.

ticket: We're getting SSL_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE when connecting to your API. This started after we rotated our client certificates.
agent_response: SSL_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE after a certificate rotation is almost always one of two things: (1) the new certificate's CN/SAN doesn't match what we have on file for your client auth, or (2) the certificate chain is incomplete — you may be sending only your leaf cert without the intermediate CA. Can you confirm which certificate you rotated — client cert for mTLS or your server-side cert — and share the certificate fingerprint? I can check what we have stored for your account against what you're sending.

ticket: Our data export job has been timing out for the past three days. It worked fine before.
agent_response: Three-day onset of timeouts on a previously stable job suggests something changed — either your data volume crossed a threshold, or something in the query path got slower. I'd rather isolate before recommending a fix. A few questions: (1) Has your record count grown significantly recently? (2) Are you filtering the export or pulling everything? (3) What timeout value are you hitting — is it your client timeout or an error from our API? Once I know that, I can tell you whether we're looking at a pagination issue, a query optimization problem, or something we need to fix on our side.

ticket: I'm getting a 500 error when I call POST /orders. It happens consistently with the same payload.
agent_response: A consistent 500 on a specific payload is much easier to debug than an intermittent one — there's a reproducible root cause. Can you share the exact payload you're sending (please redact any PII or secrets) and the full error response body? If you have a request ID from the response headers, that will let me pull the server-side stack trace directly. I want to see exactly which field or combination is triggering the failure before I speculate on the cause.

ticket: Our dashboard shows zero events for today but our backend is sending them. We have no errors in our logs.
agent_response: No errors on your side with zero events on ours points to events being dropped or rejected silently. Most common causes: (1) events sent to the wrong environment endpoint (production vs staging), (2) a timestamp so far in the future or past that they're filtered, or (3) a malformed event body that passes your client validation but fails ours. Can you copy one raw event payload you sent today and the exact endpoint URL you're posting to? I'll verify whether we received it and what happened to it.

ticket: After deploying a new version, our background jobs are failing with 'connection pool exhausted'.
agent_response: Connection pool exhaustion after a deploy almost always means the new version is either (1) not releasing connections after use — typically a missing close() call or a transaction not committed — or (2) opening more connections per request than before due to a code change. The deploy timing is the strongest signal here. Can you diff what changed in your database interaction code between versions? Also: what's your configured pool size, and how many worker instances are you running? That will tell me if the pool size is the constraint or the usage pattern is.

ticket: Random 504 gateway timeouts on our account. Other customers don't seem affected.
agent_response: Account-specific 504s are unusual — that pattern usually means something in your account's request processing path is slow or stuck, not a global infrastructure issue. I'm checking our service status now. While I do that, can you tell me: (1) which specific endpoints you're hitting when you see the 504s, and (2) what your request looks like — are these reads or writes, and roughly how large is the payload? Some 504s on account-specific paths can be caused by a data query that degrades with account size.

ticket: Our SAML SSO integration broke today. Users get redirected to a blank page after authenticating.
agent_response: A blank page after SAML authentication usually means the SP-initiated flow completed the handoff but the application couldn't process the assertion — often a malformed assertion, a clock skew issue between your IdP and our SP, or a missing attribute in the assertion that our SP expects. Can you check your IdP logs for the failing assertion and tell me: (1) what attributes your IdP is sending in the assertion, and (2) what your IdP logs show as the status of the outbound assertion? I can cross-reference against what our SP is configured to expect for your tenant.

ticket: Memory usage on our self-hosted instance keeps climbing and only restarting fixes it.
agent_response: A memory leak that only resolves on restart is a serious pattern — this isn't just tuning, something is accumulating that shouldn't be. To diagnose it properly I need to know: (1) which version of the self-hosted instance you're running, (2) roughly how long it takes to go from normal to critical memory after a restart, and (3) whether the climb correlates with specific activity (high traffic, specific operations, scheduled jobs) or is constant regardless. With that I can check if this is a known issue in your version or if we need to capture a heap dump while it's in the degraded state.

ticket: Our nightly data import job started failing at step 3 of 5. The error says 'duplicate key constraint'.
agent_response: A duplicate key violation at a consistent step suggests your import is hitting records that already exist — either the job ran partially before and left orphaned rows, or the uniqueness constraint is being applied to a field that can legitimately repeat across imports (like an external ID that's reused). Before I can tell you which, I need to know: (1) what field is the duplicate key on, and (2) did the job succeed on its previous run, or has it been failing for multiple consecutive nights? If it's been failing in a row, there may be orphaned data from the first failure that needs to be cleaned before the job can succeed.

ticket: Our file uploads over 100MB are failing. Smaller files work fine.
agent_response: A clean size threshold failure like this is almost always a configured limit — either a max body size on a reverse proxy in front of our API, a timeout that kicks in before the upload completes, or a multipart upload that isn't being chunked. The fix depends on which constraint you're hitting. Can you tell me: (1) what HTTP status code you receive when the large upload fails, and (2) does it fail immediately or partway through? An immediate failure suggests a size limit rejection; a mid-transfer failure suggests a timeout. That will tell us where the constraint is.

ticket: We're seeing inconsistent data between our primary and replica databases. Some reads return stale data.
agent_response: Replica lag is the first thing to check here, but inconsistency can also come from reading from both primary and replica without a consistent routing strategy. I want to understand the pattern before recommending anything: (1) How long does the stale data persist before catching up — seconds, minutes, or indefinitely? (2) Are you explicitly routing some reads to the replica or is this transparent load balancing? If it's indefinite staleness rather than lag, we may be looking at a replication failure rather than just lag, which is a different fix entirely.

ticket: Our GraphQL mutations succeed but the data isn't being saved.
agent_response: Mutations returning success without persisting data is a specific pattern — usually the mutation resolves successfully at the application layer but the write is being rolled back or silently dropped before it reaches the database. Common causes: a transaction being rolled back on a validation error elsewhere in the operation, or the mutation hitting a read replica instead of the primary. Can you tell me: (1) is this happening on all mutations or specific ones, and (2) what does your mutation response look like — do you get the expected data back in the response or is the response empty? That will tell me whether the write is happening and being rolled back, or not happening at all.

ticket: The search on our platform returns results for terms we know exist but says 'no results found' for others.
agent_response: Partial search failures where some terms work and others don't usually point to a tokenization or stemming issue — the way the term is broken down at index time doesn't match how it's parsed at query time. This could also be a synonym config problem or a field that isn't being indexed. To figure out which: can you give me three or four specific examples — terms that fail and terms that succeed — and tell me if the failing terms have anything in common (special characters, length, language)? I want to see the pattern before I check the index config for your account.

ticket: Emails sent through your API are being delivered to spam by Gmail. Other providers are fine.
agent_response: Gmail-specific spam placement while other providers accept the email is almost always a reputation signal specific to Gmail's filters, not an authentication issue (those would fail across all providers). Most likely causes: (1) sending domain reputation with Gmail specifically, (2) content patterns that match Gmail's spam heuristics, or (3) IP pool reputation for Gmail traffic. To diagnose: can you check the email headers of a message that landed in spam and share the Authentication-Results header and the X-Google-DKIM-Signature result? That will tell me whether Gmail's spam decision is auth-based or reputation-based.

ticket: Our Kubernetes pods running your agent keep crashing with OOMKilled after about 6 hours.
agent_response: OOMKilled at a consistent 6-hour interval is a strong signal of a leak that accumulates over time rather than a load spike. The regularity suggests a periodic process — a scheduled job, a report aggregation, or a cache that isn't being evicted — rather than request-driven growth. I'd rather confirm than guess. Can you tell me: (1) what memory limit you've set on the pod, (2) whether the memory graph shows a steady climb or a sharp spike before the kill, and (3) whether the crash timing correlates with any scheduled jobs or cron tasks in your environment? That will help me determine whether this is a known version-specific issue or something environment-specific.

ticket: Users report the app becomes unresponsive after about 30 minutes of use. No errors in our logs.
agent_response: No errors with a consistent 30-minute degradation is one of the harder patterns to diagnose remotely — it usually means the failure is silent: a deadlock, a worker thread that's blocking, or a connection that isn't timing out. The clean timer is a clue — 30 minutes often aligns with a session timeout, token expiry, or a keep-alive interval. Before I look into this on our side, can you tell me: (1) what 'unresponsive' means — does the app freeze entirely, fail specific actions, or show a spinner that never resolves, and (2) is it affecting all users simultaneously or individual user sessions independently? That split changes the diagnosis significantly.

ticket: My API calls started returning 429 errors about 2 hours ago. We haven't changed anything on our end.
agent_response: Your account is definitely being rate limited because you're sending too many requests. You need to reduce your API call frequency and implement exponential backoff in your code. This will resolve the issue.

ticket: Our webhook deliveries are failing intermittently. Maybe 20% of events don't reach our endpoint.
agent_response: The issue is that your server is rejecting our webhook requests. Please make sure your endpoint is publicly accessible and that you've whitelisted our IP addresses. Once you do that, the failures should stop.

ticket: The sync between our CRM and your platform stopped working yesterday. No error message shown.
agent_response: Silent sync failures are usually caused by your network firewall blocking our requests. Please check with your network team to ensure our IP range is whitelisted. If that doesn't fix it, try re-authenticating the integration.

ticket: Users on iOS are getting logged out randomly. Android users are fine.
agent_response: This is a known issue with iOS 17 and we're working on a fix. In the meantime, please ask your users to turn off Background App Refresh for your app. This should prevent the random logouts.

ticket: We're getting SSL_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE when connecting to your API. This started after we rotated our client certificates.
agent_response: You need to clear your SSL cache and restart your application server. SSL handshake failures after cert rotation are always caused by the old certificate being cached. A restart should clear this up immediately.

ticket: Our data export job has been timing out for the past three days. It worked fine before.
agent_response: Try running the export again. Sometimes timeouts are just transient network issues. If it continues to fail, try running it at a less busy time like early morning when server load is lower.

ticket: I'm getting a 500 error when I call POST /orders. It happens consistently with the same payload.
agent_response: Our API is experiencing some issues right now that are causing 500 errors for some customers. Our engineering team is aware and working on it. Please try again in a few hours and the issue should be resolved.

ticket: Our dashboard shows zero events for today but our backend is sending them. We have no errors in our logs.
agent_response: The dashboard sometimes has a delay in displaying events. This is a known display issue and your events are being captured correctly on our end. The dashboard should update within the next 30 minutes.

ticket: After deploying a new version, our background jobs are failing with 'connection pool exhausted'.
agent_response: You need to increase your database connection pool size. The error message is clear — you don't have enough connections. Go to your configuration file and double the pool size setting. That will fix the exhausted connection pool error.

ticket: Random 504 gateway timeouts on our account. Other customers don't seem affected.
agent_response: 504 gateway timeouts are caused by network latency between your servers and ours. Please check your network configuration and make sure you're connecting from a region close to our data centers. You may want to switch to our EU region if you're based in Europe.

ticket: Our SAML SSO integration broke today. Users get redirected to a blank page after authenticating.
agent_response: Please try clearing your browser cache and cookies and attempting to log in again. SSO issues are often caused by stale session data in the browser. If that doesn't work, try using an incognito window.

ticket: Memory usage on our self-hosted instance keeps climbing and only restarting fixes it.
agent_response: Your server doesn't have enough RAM for your workload. You should upgrade to a server with at least 32GB of RAM. Memory issues like this are always a sign of insufficient resources. I'd also recommend adding more swap space as a temporary measure.

ticket: Our nightly data import job started failing at step 3 of 5. The error says 'duplicate key constraint'.
agent_response: You need to add error handling to your import script to skip duplicate records. Use INSERT OR IGNORE or an upsert operation instead of a plain INSERT. This will prevent the constraint violation from crashing your job.

ticket: Our file uploads over 100MB are failing. Smaller files work fine.
agent_response: Your file sizes are exceeding our API limits. Our standard plan supports files up to 50MB. You'll need to upgrade to our Enterprise plan which supports files up to 5GB. Alternatively, you can compress your files before uploading.

ticket: We're seeing inconsistent data between our primary and replica databases. Some reads return stale data.
agent_response: Inconsistent data between databases is a replication failure. You need to rebuild your replica from scratch — take a full backup of your primary, restore it to the replica, and then re-enable replication. This is the only reliable way to fix data inconsistency.

ticket: Our GraphQL mutations succeed but the data isn't being saved.
agent_response: This sounds like a caching issue. GraphQL clients often cache mutation results and display cached data without actually saving it. Please check your Apollo Client or Relay configuration and make sure you're invalidating the cache after mutations.

ticket: The search on our platform returns results for terms we know exist but says 'no results found' for others.
agent_response: Search indexing can sometimes get out of sync. Please go to Settings > Search > Rebuild Index and run a full reindex. This process takes about 15–20 minutes and will fix most search inconsistencies. Let us know if it's still not working after the reindex completes.

ticket: Emails sent through your API are being delivered to spam by Gmail. Only Gmail is affected.
agent_response: Gmail is very strict about spam. The most likely cause is that your email content contains spam trigger words. Please review your email templates and remove any words like 'free', 'guarantee', 'click here', or excessive use of exclamation marks. Also make sure you're not sending too many emails at once.

ticket: Our Kubernetes pods running your agent keep crashing with OOMKilled after about 6 hours.
agent_response: OOMKilled means your pods are running out of memory. The fix is simple: increase the memory limit in your Kubernetes deployment manifest. Change your limits.memory from whatever it currently is to at least 4Gi. This will give the agent enough headroom to operate without being killed.

ticket: Users report the app becomes unresponsive after about 30 minutes of use. No errors in our logs.
agent_response: Please have your users refresh the page or log out and back in after 30 minutes. This sounds like a normal session management behavior. You can also try increasing your session timeout setting to 60 minutes to avoid the issue.
